doc.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Being choosy in studio work and doubling
summary: A player can be choosy only if in demand; he doubles on clarinet, flutes and piccolo and would like to teach schools with big band charts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Are you able to be, with the studio work, be choosy if you want to be?
Well you are always able to be choosy, the other question is can you make a living being choosy. Not very much. You have to be quite in demand and maybe in demand for some

kind of music that is popular. But no, you more or less have to be available. I was trying to play all the doubles and like the clarinet and the bass clarinet and the bass flute and the piccolo and the alto flute. I have them all. But you have to, more or less to make a good living in the studio you have to make an effort to play anything that comes along. But I want to play more live. I like doing things like we did last night. I like to play schools, bring some big band charts along and teach the sax section how to play. I’ve done — I don’t do much of that but I’d like to do more of that. Get a good collection of some big band charts that I like to play.
